title: The Storm Eater reborn
summary: How a bound Bane became a fusion of Weaver and Wyrm.

claims.text: Few Garou know of the Storm Eater, and fewer recall when its Uktena binders chained it; once it had fed on Wyld energy until it grew vast, then lay dormant for ages unable to call its minions.
In the 1830s the Europeans’ seizure of too many Uktena and Wendigo caerns weakened the seals, and the Bane slipped out and began feeding again.
Its stirring woke a mighty Weaver-spirit drawn by its size, and the two merged into a new entity that burst into the High Umbra; its spawn carry traits of both parents.
European Garou have alienated the natives who might remember the Bane’s binding, and the native tribes are too pressed defending their lands to hunt it.

title: The lost tribes of the frontier era
summary: The Croatan’s sacrifice and the Bunyip’s fading.

claims.text: The Croatan, one of the three first tribes of the Pure Lands, lived along the eastern seaboard until the Eater-of-Souls came with the Roanoke colonists; they and all their Kinfolk gave their lives in a rite that drove it from the physical world.
The Uktena and Wendigo still mourn them and fear the spread of Wyrm-tainted settlers means a similar end for themselves.
In Australia the Bunyip dwindle as settlers take their land and hunt their thylacine Kin, and before the century ends they will be gone.
The Tribe Novel Children of Gaia and Uktena tells that many Wendigo, youngest of the three Pure tribes, blame the Uktena for failing to save the Croatan.

title: Caerns on the frontier
summary: Who holds the power sites of the Savage West.

claims.text: Caerns in or near towns usually fall to the Iron Riders or Bone Gnawers, the tribes most at ease among humans; people avoid such places without knowing why and call them haints.
A few urban caerns exist among settled Uktena Kinfolk, kept as special kivas or sweat lodges inside the community and reserved for spirit messengers.

title: The Get of Fenris in the West
summary: How the Get see the Pure Ones and the frontier.

claims.text: The Get hold that only the strongest deserve to survive, and blame the Uktena and Wendigo for growing too weak to keep the Wyrm or the Get off their land.
They favour the cold north, which recalls their homelands and pits them directly against the Wendigo.

title: Staredown (Wild West)
summary: A level two Gift for the stand-off.

claims.text: With only a look into a target’s eyes, the Garou makes the target flinch, often drop the gun and flee in terror.
Used on a Garou, it makes the target freeze in place instead of running; a Ram-spirit is one teacher.
